# Kardlings

> A Kardling card is a 384x576 PNG that carries, in its top 16 pixel rows, a sealed recipe for a small working mind (a
> scorecard of at most six readable rules over one department's records), the signed history of its owners, and every
> level it has earned. Opened on any device, it grows that mind there, offline, and proves its score on cases it never
> grew on. It can be owned, given (re-signed), fused (a fused card is kept only if it beats both parents) and coupled into a
> mesh whose ledger credits each owner by measured contribution. Every claim on it can be re-run.

Live page: https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/kardlings/
Source: https://github.com/sjgant80-hub/kardlings (MIT — no licence fee)

## Key facts
- The genesis drop: genesis cards across the departments of five public datasets that cleared a 0.6 AUC bar on GATE;
  decoder #0001 re-runs the whole drop (it names the decoder's hash and the genesis log's head).
- A level is earned only by a search that beats the mind by 0.002 AUC on GATE; its receipt re-runs exactly.
- Ownership: the last signed give names the owner; a double sale is refused by the registry (first recorded give wins).
- Nothing is neural; nothing is sent anywhere; records never leave the device.
- Every kernel is mutation-gated (witness); every organ was sealed before it was measured (git proves the order).
- The page opens as a pixel game view built from the cards' own art engine: eight screens (Estate, Base, Cards,
  Evals, Mint, Mesh, Send, Proof) over the same kernels; the classic document view holds the full explanation.
- A player's key is never kept in browser storage: it lives in the open tab and in the key file they save.
- FallWorld, the agent economy as a game: every card is born with two node slots (more as it levels) and two tool slots.
  Nodes are the owner's own cards of other departments, coupled with it and joining only if they measurably add; tools
  are the estate's proven apps as signed items, and move no score.
- Arena: two cards fight on 64 GATE cases drawn from both owners' signatures, each as it is kitted; the receipt re-runs;
  nothing is staked. Raids: unsolved departments struck by signed searches (the first to clear 0.6 seals the first card);
  world bosses (a whole business) cleared only by a party of owners' cards, each member's measured share on the record.
- The record: a player's releases and party shares as entries of the estate's contribution ledger (internal units, not
  money; the switch off).

## The talker

Any Kardling card can be asked in plain words on its Talker screen. It answers yes or no about one case only from the rules that fired, says how it decides and how good it is, and otherwise abstains and says what it would need: it never makes an answer up, and the same question always gets the same answer with a receipt. Organ 14 measured it on 1,500 GATE rows said in words.

## Builds and combos

A build is a few Kardlings put to one job together: one card per department of a business, the player's own or the drop's. The device measures it on GATE cases none of them grew on: a build that beats its best card by 0.005 or more is a combo, one that does worse by as much an anti-combo, and each card shows what it adds or why it sits on the bench. Two different keys measuring it again to the very same numbers prove it; the first found it. A build can be shrunk into one small card, kept only if it beats every card it came from by 0.002. Nothing is staked.

## The guild

Friends can stand together in a guild on the estate screen: each signs a join with their own key, carrying their estate, and the guild draws every member's estate side by side. Nobody can join anybody else, a later leave takes a member out, and a guild moves no card, no rating and no credit. A signature proves who said it, not that it is so, so cards of the drop are checked against the drop. Organ 15 measured it on 400 seeded guilds.
